annotations.title: Check a value against cited limits

description: Is a measured value over the limits we hold? Give a parameter, a number and its unit (and a place, medium or statistic to narrow). Every row find_limits would return comes back with a verdict: over, within, under (below a floor or a band's bottom), or not_comparable with a `why` (a unit of another family or one we never convert, a number that depends on the water's hardness, pH or temperature, an equation or narrative, a value printed for reference, a row under a longer parameter name). Units convert exactly within a family (µg/L to mg/L); no limit is summed or inferred. `counts` totals the verdicts over all rows. Quote each row's `cite`; whether its statistic and conditions are yours is for you to say.

medium.description: What the limit governs: an effluent (water_discharge), the receiving water (surface_water), groundwater, air.

offset.description: Where the next page starts (the answer's next_offset); rows come over first, then under, within, not_comparable.

parameter.description: The substance or measure as a regulation names it (copper, ammonia, pH) or its CAS number.

place.description: ISO 3166 code of where the rule binds: a country (US, CA, DE, FR, IT), a state or province (US-OH, CA-QC), or EU. A place also searches every place above it: US-OH searches US-OH and US; DE searches DE and EU. Omit to search everywhere.

statistic.description: Only rows under this statistic: daily_max, monthly_avg, instant, composite, ...

unit.description: The value's unit: mg/L, µg/L (or ug/L, mg L-1), ng/L, mg/kg, µg/m³, pH (or SU) ...

value.description: The measured value, one number (0.15). A decimal string is read too, with a point or one decimal comma (0,15); 1,500 is refused as ambiguous.

name: check_value
title: Check a value against cited limits
